pr.title: Git - support for SHA-256 repositories (#227281)
pr.body:
Fixes #227281

## Credit

This builds on @PositroniumJS’s work in #317363. Their two commits are preserved with authorship intact, and this PR supersedes that one.

The original investigation and hash-pattern updates are theirs. This PR carries that work forward and fixes the remaining SHA-256 blame truncation.

## Problem

The proposed blame pattern matches the 40-character alternative first:

```ts
/^([0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64})/gm
```

Because no delimiter follows the group, a SHA-256 object ID matches only its first 40 characters.

The truncated value becomes `BlameInformation.hash`. It cannot match the full IDs returned by `getUnpublishedCommits()`, causing the blame hover to offer remote commands for unpublished commits.

## Changes

- Introduce a shared, grouped object-ID pattern with the 64-character alternative first:

  ```ts
  const OBJECT_ID = '(?:[0-9a-f]{64}|[0-9a-f]{40})';
  ```

  Use it across the affected parsers and reuse `objectIdRegex` for Git operation validation and blame’s full-hash checks. Preserve the validator’s existing zero-ID handling.

- Extract `getRemoteRefs` parsing into `parseLsRemote` for direct testing and reuse of the shared pattern. This preserves the base implementation’s existing branch-name/hash mapping and SHA-1/SHA-256 support.

- Raise the maximum `git.commitShortHashLength` from 40 to 64.

- Add SHA-256 commit/tree cases and direct tests for object-ID matching, blame, refs, remote refs, and stashes. Include SHA-1 cases to protect existing behavior.

## Verification

Local checks during the rebase and subsequent review:

- Passed 31 selected existing parser tests using an in-memory harness that executes the TypeScript source after stripping types.
- Confirmed that restoring the shorter-first alternation makes both SHA-256 blame regression tests fail.
- Checked real SHA-1 and SHA-256 repository output, including merge commits, blame ranges, annotated/lightweight tags, remote refs, multiple stashes, and detached HEAD files.
- After sharing the validator’s regex, reran both object-ID tests and verified equivalent acceptance, rejection, and error messages across 24,507 cases.

Full TypeScript checking and the extension-host Mocha suite have not been rerun locally after the rebase.

## Scope

This PR addresses the Git extension. SHA-256 assumptions elsewhere in the repository, including build tooling, remain outside its scope.

reviews.body:
## Pull request overview

Adds SHA-256 object ID support across the Git extension while preserving SHA-1 compatibility.

**Changes:**
- Updates Git output parsers and blame handling for 64-character IDs.
- Corrects remote branch parsing and expands short-hash configuration.
- Adds SHA-1/SHA-256 parser tests.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `extensions/git/src/git.ts` | Updates object ID parsing and remote ref handling. |
| `extensions/git/src/blame.ts` | Recognizes SHA-256 IDs in blame resources. |
| `extensions/git/src/test/git.test.ts` | Adds parser coverage for both hash formats. |
| `extensions/git/package.json` | Raises the short-hash maximum to 64. |




<details>
<summary>Comments suppressed due to low confidence (2)</summary>

**extensions/git/src/git.ts:1062**
* The stash parser repeats the 40/64-character alternatives rather than consuming `OBJECT_ID`, so the supposedly centralized object-id definition can drift from this parser. Construct this regex from `OBJECT_ID` too.
```
const stashRegex = /([0-9a-f]{64}|[0-9a-f]{40})\n(.*)\nstash@{(\d+)}\n(WIP\s)?on\s([^:]+):\s(.*)\n(\d+)\n(\d+)(?:\x00)/gmi;
```
**extensions/git/src/git.ts:1313**
* This third copy of the object-id alternatives defeats the single-pattern design: changes to `OBJECT_ID` will not reach ref parsing. Interpolate the noncapturing `OBJECT_ID` fragment so the existing capture indexes remain unchanged.
```
	const refRegex = /^(refs\/[^\0]+)\0([0-9a-f]{64}|[0-9a-f]{40})\0([0-9a-f]{64}|[0-9a-f]{40})?(?:\0(.*))?$/gm;
```
</details>

commit.message: fix: Git - change regexp to be compatible with SHA256 commits (#227281)
Add tests for SHA-256 hash commits

fix: preserve full SHA-256 object IDs in blame

Match the 64-character alternative first so SHA-256 blame hashes are not
truncated to 40 characters. Keeping full hashes restores comparisons with
getUnpublishedCommits and prevents remote hover commands from appearing
for unpublished commits.

Share a grouped OBJECT_ID pattern across the commit, stash, blame, ref,
remote-ref and detached-HEAD parsers. Reuse objectIdRegex for Git operation
validation and blame's full-hash checks. The pattern uses separate 64- and
40-character alternatives.

Extract getRemoteRefs parsing into parseLsRemote and add direct parser
tests, preserving the existing branch-name and commit-hash mapping.

Allow git.commitShortHashLength values up to 64. Add SHA-1 and SHA-256
regression tests for object IDs, blame ranges, refs, remote refs and
stashes.
